name: Data protection by EU institutions Regulation
impact_assessment: none (relied on the GDPR impact assessment SEC(2012) 72)
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission self-assessment based on a survey of EU bodies; no independent studies found
summary: These rules bring data protection in the EU institutions in line with the GDPR. The Commission's 2022 review, based on a survey of 56 EU bodies, judged them to be working well: over half gave their data protection officers more resources and routine checks by the supervisor fell as intended, but the supervisor had not issued any fines. No independent study has assessed the rules' effects.

indicators.objective: Ensure consistent application of data protection rules throughout the Union (alignment of EU institutions' rules with the GDPR)
Rationalise the governance model and strengthen compliance and enforcement in EU institutions and bodies

indicators.indicator: Number of opinions issued by the EDPB and the EDPS
indicators.evidence: Reported qualitatively: EDPS replies to legislative consultations with opinions and comments; EDPB output growing. No time series tied to the Regulation.

indicators.indicator: Breakdown of activities of data protection officers
indicators.evidence: Survey of 56 EU bodies: 54% gave more resources to DPOs; 84% adapted processes so staff consult DPOs. No breakdown of DPO activities.

indicators.indicator: Use made of data protection impact assessments
indicators.evidence: Annex table of DPIAs by institution 2019-2021 (most by ECB, EIB and Commission); cases sent to the EDPS fell sharply compared with the old prior-checking system, as intended; 94% of bodies find DPIA criteria adequate.

indicators.indicator: Number of complaints made by data subjects
indicators.evidence: Report notes inadmissible complaints to the EDPS rose 2019-2021 (mostly aimed at national controllers); no clear trend in requests from individuals because institutions record them differently.

indicators.indicator: Fines imposed on data controllers responsible for breaches
indicators.evidence: None: by 2022 the EDPS had used most powers (e.g. temporary processing bans) but had never issued a fine.

indicators.objective: No dedicated impact assessment: the proposal (COM(2017) 8) relied on the GDPR impact assessment and gave no quantified forecasts

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), First report on the application of the Data Protection Regulation for EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (Regulation 2018/1725), COM(2022) 530
literature.title: First report on the application of the Data Protection Regulation for EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (Regulation 2018/1725)
literature.method: review (survey of 56 EU bodies, EDPS contribution)
literature.headline: Regulation 'working well and fit for purpose'; 54% of bodies gave more resources to DPOs; DPIAs replaced prior checking and cut routine consultations of the EDPS; EDPS had not used its power to fine; proposes aligning rules for Europol/Eurojust/EPPO
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the rules for EU institutions work well: bodies invested more in data protection officers and risk assessments, and the supervisor used bans but never fines.
literature.quality: self-evaluation based on self-reported survey; no outcome measures

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Staff working document accompanying the Digital Omnibus proposals, SWD(2025) 836
literature.title: Staff working document accompanying the Digital Omnibus proposals
literature.headline: Proposes mirroring the Omnibus GDPR amendments in Regulation 2018/1725 to keep EU-institution rules aligned with the GDPR; no new evidence on the Regulation's effects
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's 2025 simplification package would change these rules in step with planned GDPR changes, but presents no new evidence on how they have worked.
literature.quality: policy document; no ex-post data on EUDPR

literature.title: Results of the Survey on the designation and position of the data protection officer in the EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
literature.method: supervisory questionnaire survey, 69 responses covering 71 EU institutions, bodies and agencies (March 2023)
literature.outcomes: DPO resources, independence, involvement, compliance with Regulation 2018/1725
literature.headline: Almost half of the 69 DPOs say their resources are insufficient, 30% have no full-time-equivalent support and under 30% have their own budget, while most are consulted on 75-100% of data protection issues; 3 of 69 (4%) report being penalised for their work.
literature.summary_plain: The EU's own data protection watchdog surveyed privacy officers in EU bodies: they are generally consulted and listened to, but many lack staff and time, which risks weakening data protection inside EU institutions.
literature.period_geography: EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, 2023
literature.quality: Self-reported supervisory survey with near-full coverage; descriptive, no before/after comparison.
literature.interested_party: EDPS is the supervisor under the Regulation
literature.citation: European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) (2024), Results of the Survey on the designation and position of the data protection officer in the EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, EDPS report (Coordinated Enforcement Action 2023)
